meta.commit_sha: unknown (no git log run during audit)

items.name: Entity Existence Gate — depth() Pattern
items.description: depth() returns -1 if entity not found anywhere in the chain, distinguishing 'empty blast radius' from 'entity does not exist'. Prevents impact_analysis false-green for non-existent entities.
items.cortex_application: Pre-flight existence check in impact_analysis: if entity not in index, return NOT_FOUND rather than empty dependents.
items.counter_case: Cortex entity lookup is already a Map read; the -1 sentinel adds no new capability over `entity !== undefined`. Value is disciplined naming, not novel logic.
items.proposed_phase: Fix for existing flaw #2 — no new phase needed

items.name: Atomic Singleton State — StateLink
items.description: StateLink(alias, body) enforces uniqueness: exactly one StateLink per alias. Inserting a new one atomically removes the old one. Thread-safe: observers always see old or new, never zero.
items.cortex_application: save_entity/save_concept as atomic replacement (never duplicate). lastSyncCommit as singleton slot. soulDirty flag initialized in a defined slot to avoid cold-start undefined reads.
items.counter_case: Cortex state is file-based. Atomic replacement requires write-then-rename at the filesystem level, not in-memory pointer swap. Pattern transfers conceptually but needs different implementation substrate.
items.proposed_phase: Fixes for flaws #4, #16, #19 — no new phase needed

items.name: Diagnostic Comparison — content_compare with emit_diagnostics
items.description: content_compare(first, second, check_values=true, emit_diagnostics=true) dumps a line-by-line diff of every atom and value key that differs between two spaces. Single boolean flag converts correctness check to actionable diff.
items.cortex_application: impact_analysis version diff: show which fields changed (role, interface, relationships), not just 'changed: true'.
items.counter_case: Cortex entities are markdown strings; structural diff is text diff. Output quality depends on entity format structure.

items.name: Transient COW Knowledge Frame for Dry-Run
items.description: push_frame() creates a COW child AtomSpace. All mutations in the child are invisible to the parent. pop_frame() discards child entirely. Parent untouched unless caller explicitly promotes changes.
items.cortex_application: compress(dry_run=true): snapshot .knowledge/ in memory, run compression, collect diff, discard. Only compress(apply=true) writes to disk. Same pattern for ingest preview.
items.counter_case: Simpler: collect all intended mutations as a list, display, then conditionally apply. COW adds isolation preventing half-applied states, but Cortex file operations can be aborted by not calling fs.writeFile.
items.proposed_phase: Fix for flaw #44 — no new phase needed

items.name: Active Architecture Design-Notes Pattern
items.description: Four committed design documents capture active debates, failed approaches, and explicit design flaws. Living documents, not historical artifacts.
items.cortex_application: Create design-notes/ dir with committed .md files for each major design debate. Update Librarian synthesis prompt to populate failedApproaches from these documents.
items.counter_case: Free-form design docs are less queryable than structured failedApproaches fields. The real fix for flaw #113 is updating the Librarian prompt.
items.proposed_phase: Fix for flaw #113 — no new phase needed

items.name: Thread-Local Resource Pool — EvaluatorPool
items.description: thread_local map keyed by AtomSpacePtr. Each thread gets its own evaluator; no shared mutex for dispatch. RAII eval_dtor (lines 110-118) returns evaluators to shared pool on thread exit.
items.cortex_application: source tool AST skeleton cache: thread_local Map<string, CacheEntry> as hot layer keyed by (entityId, version). Each parallel call gets isolated read path; falls through to shared cache on miss.
items.counter_case: Flaw #46's root cause is shared write path (skeleton computation + invalidation). Thread-local read caches don't help if both calls trigger a write. Real fix is making write path idempotent.
items.proposed_phase: Fix for flaw #46 — no new phase needed

items.name: TypeIndex — O(1) Type-Based Entity Queries
items.description: std::vector<AtomSet> indexed by Type integer. Each AtomSet is an unordered_set<Handle> + shared_mutex. O(1) 'all atoms of type X' query. Benchmark note: std::unordered_set over Folly F14 (race conditions in pattern matcher).
items.cortex_application: Add typeIndex: Map<string, Set<string>> to in-memory state. Update on every save_entity/save_concept. cortex_find with type filter becomes O(1) set lookup.
items.counter_case: Cortex KB is small (<200 entities); linear scan is fast in practice. Type index adds write overhead. Premature optimization unless performance is already a complaint.
items.proposed_phase: Phase 13.5.3 — TypeIndex for Entity Category Queries

items.name: ODR Dedup Guard for Plugin Registration
items.description: _loaded_modules set check in beginTypeDecls() prevents double-registration when library loaded from both build dir and system dir.
items.cortex_application: Set<string> _registeredTools check in MCP tool registration path. If tool name already registered, skip with warning. Prevents silent overwrites in dev/hot-reload.
items.counter_case: MCP servers typically restart on hot-reload; double-registration may never occur in practice.

items.name: Selectivity-First ('Thinnest Term') Search Ordering
items.description: Start search from constant with smallest incoming set (most selective). Prunes search space early — same insight as SQL query planners and Datalog magic sets.
items.cortex_application: For multi-term cortex_find, estimate selectivity per term (term doc frequency from fuzzy index), order most-to-least selective, intersect results. First term produces smallest candidate set.
items.counter_case: Cortex entity corpus is small; multi-term search completes in <5ms. Selectivity ordering adds complexity for marginal savings. More relevant after Phase 33.5 (SQLite FTS5).

items.name: FutureStream — Lazy Computed Entity Properties
items.description: _formula executed in _scratch AtomSpace on each tap. Results don't pollute base space. Lazy: no computation until tapped.
items.cortex_application: computedProperties field in entity schema. Each entry is a formula reference. read_entity executes formula against current entity state. Results never written to disk — always current.
items.counter_case: Quality scores already recomputed on read by get_entity_quality. Generic formula system adds complexity without immediate payoff.

items.name: QueueValue — Async Streaming Pipeline
items.description: Thread-safe FIFO with open()/close()/add()/remove() lifecycle. Producer-consumer API with explicit open/close state.
items.cortex_application: Long-running tools (ingest, compress, synthesis) return streamId immediately. Caller polls stream_read(streamId). Queue open while running, closed when done.
items.counter_case: MCP protocol doesn't natively support streaming responses. Requires Phase 22 (central server). Progress can be approximated with log output in CLI context.
items.proposed_phase: Phase 22.2 — Streaming Results for Long-Running Operations

items.name: Key-value properties per entity
items.cortex_superior_because: Cortex entity schema has persistence, serialization, git-tracked history. AtomSpace KVPMap is in-memory only.
items.steel_man: AtomSpace KVPMap supports any Value type including nested streams; Cortex's string-serialized properties can't represent computed or lazy values.

items.name: Pattern compile-once-run-many
items.cortex_superior_because: Cortex's pattern cache is lighter-weight; no N! permutation explosion, no virtual link overhead.
items.steel_man: AtomSpace's engine handles arbitrary graph topology including disconnected components and optional clauses. Needed if Cortex ever supports 'find X that references Y but not Z within 2 hops'.

items.reason: No TS equivalent; violates Cortex principle #1 (local-first complexity)

items.reason: Phase 22+ territory; requires server for scale; N! worst case

items.name: ContentHash Merkle-tree atom identity
items.reason: Major redesign of Cortex filepath-based entity identity; violates principle #4 (derived data)

items.name: Unordered link permutation search (N! worst case)
items.reason: Acknowledged AtomSpace bug (#1502). Not a pattern to adopt.

items.name: Reader-Writer Mutex Overhead Anti-Pattern
items.pattern: Adding RWMutex to shared caches on assumption 'many readers, few writers' justifies abstraction. Profiling shows RW mutexes frequently worse due to cache-line ping-ponging.
items.proposed_action: CLAUDE.md addition: do not add reader-writer locks to shared caches without profiling on actual workload.
items.why_target_chose_it: They tried RW mutexes, measured the failure, and documented it. NameServer now uses plain std::mutex.

items.name: Hardcoded Resource Capacity
items.pattern: MAX_NUM_VALUE = 64 compile-time constant caps type registry. Exceeding requires source change + recompilation. Same pattern as Cortex flaw #109 (10MB diff limit, 180-day stale threshold).
items.proposed_action: Cross-reference flaw #109. Make capacity limits configurable via env var or config.json.
items.why_target_chose_it: Fixed-size array avoids allocation at type registration time. No equivalent trade-off in JS Map/Set.

items.name: Integer vs String Entity Type Codes
items.question: Should Cortex adopt integer type codes + NameServer-style registry for entity types, or keep string-based types?
alternatives: Keep string types — human-readable, no registry, flexible; O(n) subtype checks
Integer codes + registry — O(1) subtype checks, type inheritance, compact; requires NameServer equivalent; brittle for dynamic extension
Hybrid — strings at API surface, integer codes internally

items.name: Reverse-Reference Index Need
items.question: Does impact_analysis need a reverse-reference index (AtomSpace InSetMap equivalent) to be correct, or is forward-reference traversal sufficient?
alternatives: Keep forward-only — simpler, correct for DAGs; fails for cycles without full traversal
Add reverse index on write — incomingSet[entityId] = Set<dependents>, O(1) blast-radius lookup; adds write overhead
Lazy reverse index — build on first impact_analysis call, cache until next write
